newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says fee levels on meat cutting operations limited.
newsitem.headline: Court says fee levels on meat cutting operations limited.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday that a decision taken by the Council of Ministers in 1988 sets fees only for meat which is actually boned or cut during the stage between slaughter and storage.

A question arose between Dutch agricultural authorities and a poultry processer in the Netherlands. After insolvency by the processor, a dispute arose over fees for the inspection of its cutting plant.

The processor only cut and boned about 5 percent of its chickens, but the Dutch inspection authorities calculated fees on the basis of the weight of all the chickens which were placed in the room where the cutting took place.

The court said the decision "determines the levels of the fees to be charged for inspections and controls connected with cutting operations...there can be no question of a member state which considers the standard levels fixed in the decision insufficient to cover the costs of inspections and controls interpreting article 3(1) of decision 88/408 in the way advocated by the Netherlands Government..."
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Dutch)
"Health inspections and controls - Circumstances in which an undertaking is obliged to pay the fee for cutting operations"
Reference from the College van Beroep voor het Bedrijsleven (Netherlands) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
H.J.A.M. van Iersel (liquidator of Pluimvee en wildwerkende industrie De Venhorst BV)
Staatssecretaris van Landbouw, Natuurbeheer en Visserij

on the interpretation of Council decision 88/408/EEC of 15 June 1988 on the levels of the fees to be charged for health inspections and controls of fresh meat pursuant to directive 85/73/EEC (OJ 1988 L 194, p. 24)

Article 3(1) of Council decision 88/408/EEC of 15 June 1988 on the levels of the fees to be charged for health inspections and controls of fresh meat pursuant to directive 85/73/EEC is to be interpreted as meaning that the part of the fees referred to therein is payable only in respect of meat which is actually boned or cut during the production stage between the slaughter of the animal and the storage of the meat.
